title: Winter Games
build: Epyx original, PAL, two disk sides (C64 Preservation Project, verified dump)

records.c: Ski Jump starts here, as the other events do: interrupts off, the stack reset, $083D set to say the menu was loaded over, the BASIC ROM banked out ($01 = $26), bitmap mode with multicolour in the video chip's bank 2 ($8000-$BFFF), the CIAs' interrupts and timers off, port A of CIA 1 set to input, a black border and background, and the raster interrupt through the KERNAL's IRQ vector ($0314) at sj_irq. Then it copies the 24 small skier shapes from $7488 to $8400-$89FF, where the sprite pointers $10 to $27 find them, and sets the interrupt for line 250.

The raster interrupt, twice a frame. At line 241 it switches to text mode with the character set at $9800 (the ROM's upper and lower case set), so the bottom row is text, and sets the next interrupt for line 251.

At line 251: bitmap mode and multicolour again for the scene, or, once the score is shown ($1C set), text mode stays and the background turns light blue. Then a step of the sound engine (sound_step), the next interrupt at line 241, the frame flag at $10, and the joystick (read_stick).
Acknowledges the raster interrupt, restores the registers the KERNAL's handler saved, and returns.

The joystick into $1D, its bits turned over so a set bit is a direction held (1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, $10 fire): port 2 with one joystick ($087D) or for odd-numbered players, port 1 for the others.

Sounds stopped, then sound 0, the event's tune; the first player and the first of three attempts ($70 and $71 both 1). Then the main loop, once a frame: by the state in $11, set up the hill (sj_setup), run the jump (sj_run), or after it (sj_after).
An RTS nothing reaches.
After a jump. In practice ($081D negative) "PLAY AGAIN?" at column 20 with YES or NO beside it: up chooses YES, down NO, fire confirms; YES jumps again, NO goes back to the menu.
Fire on the play-again question: YES (the Y at $83E0) sets state 0 for another jump; NO falls to the exit.
State 0: the hill is set up again on the next frame.
In competition: the next player ($70 counts from 1 to the number of players in $081E, $72 steps through their 32-byte records), one jump each, and after the last player the next round.
After the last player: the next of three rounds ($71) from the first player, or after the third, the scores stored and back to the menu.
The third round over: each player's best total turned into the menu's score (store_scores), then the exit.
Back to the menu: the stack reset and the loader's $0900, which loads the menu and starts it where it left off.
The question and its two answers for print_bottom, each a column then the text and a zero: "PLAY AGAIN?" at column 20, "YES   " and "NO    " at column 32.
Prints a string on the bottom text row ($83C0): its first byte is the column, then the characters (ASCII, which the ROM's second set shows as capitals) to a zero.

For every player, the best total of the three jumps as the menu ranks it: the six characters at +$10 in the player's record (" 225.9", say) become two bytes of decimal digits, the hundreds and tens at +$17 and the units and tenths at +$16. A player with no score (a zero at +$11) has "   0.0" and three zeros written at +$10 instead.
The score of a player with none: "   0.0" and three zeros.
A digit character's value; a space counts as 0.
LDX #60 before wait_frames, an entry for a wait of 60 frames that nothing calls; the other events have the same two bytes.
Waits X frames.
Waits X frames, then until fire is pressed, a frame at a time.
Waits for the frame flag at $10, which the interrupt sets once a frame, and clears it.
Unpacks each stream in the list at ($16), two bytes an address, to a zero.

Unpacks one stream from ($14): two bytes of destination address, then runs, each a count byte (0 means 64) whose top two bits say what follows: 0 one byte repeated, 1 that many bytes copied, 2 that many bytes skipped, 3 that many bytes each followed by two zeros. A zero count byte ends it.
Steps the destination pointer at $12-$13.
Steps the source pointer at $14-$15.

State 0, a jump set up: the variables at $10-$6F cleared, the sprites' colours and places from the tables below, the drift unset ($33 = $FF), 20 style points ($3F), the skier at the top of the in-run (x 64, y 50) at 1.25 pixels a frame, the in-run's script at ramp_points, a flight speed of 60 ($23) and sprites 1 to 4 showing shapes $3C to $3F. Then the hill (show_hill), a wait for any move of the stick or the button, the attempt's number cleared, state 1, sounds stopped, and sound 5 for the in-run.
For $D025-$D02E: sprite multicolours 7 and 2, and all eight sprites black.

For $D000-$D010: the skier (sprite 0) at x 64, y 50 at the top of the in-run; sprites 1 to 4, the close-up's skier, in a square of two by two at x 264 and 288, y 66 and 87 (the top bits in $D010 = $1E); sprites 5 to 7 at 0.
Nine spaces at column 20, over "ATTEMPT" and its number.
State 1, once a frame: the jump's phase (run_phase), the skier's sprite placed (place_skier), the count in $43 run down, and a step of the random number.

The hill, the first scene: its bitmap, screen and colours unpacked (hill_list), the line above the text row cleared (clear_line), the player's name (print_player), only the skier's sprite on, frame 0 drawn, and in competition "ATTEMPT" with the round's number at column 28. Then the screen on.
"ATTEMPT" at column 20, for print_bottom.

The landing slope, the second scene, with the screen off while it is drawn: its bitmap, screen and colours (flight_list), the line above the text cleared, the name, all eight sprites on, the skier back at the left edge (x 0, y $54) at one pixel a frame, the close-up's sprites past x 255, and the frame drawn. Then the screen on.

The player's name and country (16 characters from the player's record at $0800 + $72) at the left of the bottom row, spaces to its end, and, once the player has a score, the best total so far (six characters from +$10) at column 32.
Clears the bottom line of pixels of bitmap row 23 (every eighth byte from $BCC7, 40 of them), just above the text row.
The skier's x position ($25-$27, a fraction, the pixel and the top bit) moves on by the speed in $28-$2A.
On the in-run, for each whole pixel moved since the last frame ($3C), the slope's step in $35 is added to y's fraction ($2B-$2C), so the skier follows the track down.
The in-run's acceleration ($24) added to the speed ($28-$29).
The skier's y position ($2B-$2C) moves by the vertical speed ($2D-$2E).
The pull in $35-$36 added to the vertical speed, so the skier falls faster each frame.
Puts the skier's sprite at x $26 (with the top bits of $D010 set to $DF once past 255) and y $2C.
Runs the jump's phase in $38 through phase_table.
The eight phases: 0 the in-run, 1 the take-off, 2 the flight, 3 a good landing, 4 the run-out after it, 5 a fall, 6 sliding to a stop after it, 7 a missed take-off.
The phases' addresses' high bytes, read one on from phase_table.

Phase 0, down the in-run: the skier moves, follows the slope, speeds up, and takes the track's points (ramp_script). Past x 255, on the lip, fire takes off: sound 6 for the wind, phase 1, a small upward speed (-1/4 of a pixel a frame), a pull of 4/256 a frame, and frame 5. Fire before the lip does nothing, so a button held from the start takes off on the lip's first frame.

No fire: once the skier is 30 pixels past x 255 the take-off is missed: phase 7, the tumble's frames (missed_script), no upward speed and a heavy pull of $27, and the speed back to 1.25 pixels a frame.

Phase 1, off the lip on the hill's scene: the skier moves and falls under the pull; at the top of the arc (no vertical speed) frame 6, the flying pose. Once past x 335, at the hill's right edge, the landing slope's scene (show_flight), phase 2, a 180-frame wait before the skier comes into view ($32), the lean centred ($3A = $80) and the landing's frames waiting in the script pointer.

Phase 2, the flight: frames spent out of the centred pose (frame 6) counted in $34. For the first 180 frames the small skier waits off the left edge; then he glides down (air_step), and when the flight's speed ($23) has fallen to 40 he lands. Each frame the drift tips the lean ($3A), the stick pushes it back, and the lean picks the frame drawn.

The drift on the lean (drift), then the stick. Bit 1 of the drift ($33) picks the axis: clear, right adds to the lean and left takes away; set, down adds and up takes away. Each push moves it 2, or 3 against the drift's own direction. The lean's band (lean_bucket) then picks a frame from lean_frames_lr, or lean_frames_ud when the bit is set, and draws it if it changed.
Touch-down. Frame 6, the centred pose, is a good landing: sound 7 and phase 3. Any other pose is a fall: sound 8, the fall's frames (fall_script) and phase 5.

Back in the centred pose after frames out of it ($34): the drift is cleared ($33 = $FF) for drift to draw another, the style loses the penalty for the worst lean since the last return ($40, from lean_penalties), and the lean is set back to the middle.
Keeps the lean between 4 and 251, then the distance and the close-up's readout (flight_distance).
Style points lost on coming back to the centre, by the worst lean reached: 0, 2, 4 or 8.
Phase 3, a good landing: the skier glides down (air_step) with the landing's frames until he reaches the run-out at y 206, then phase 4.

Phase 4, the run-out: the skier moves on with the landing's frames; once past x 255 he slows by 12/256 of a pixel a frame. When he stops: sound 11 for a jump of 62 metres or more ($21), sound 10 for a shorter one; frame 17, arms up; 150 frames; at least 6 style points; then the score and state 2.
Phase 5, a fall: the fall's frames as the skier drops (air_step) to the run-out at y 206, then phase 6.
Phase 6, sliding to a stop after a fall, slowing by 12/256 of a pixel a frame; then 120 frames, 18 style points taken away (none left if fewer), the score and state 2.
Phase 7, the missed take-off: the skier tumbles off the lip under the heavy pull with the tumble's frames. When they end, sound 9, 120 frames, and state 2 with no score.

The drift on the lean. When none is set ($33 negative) and the flight's speed is still 44 or more, a new one is drawn from the random number's first byte: two bits, bit 0 its direction (set, the lean grows) and bit 1 the stick's axis; the count of frames out of the centre ($34) starts again. Then each frame the lean moves one step in the drift's direction.

The skier through the air: x moves by the speed, y by the vertical speed, and the pull adds to the vertical speed. Below y 160, over the slope, the vertical speed loses 10/256 and the speed gains 6/256 each frame, so he follows the ground.
The lean's band, 0 to 8, into $3D: the first of bucket_limits the lean is below.
The tops of the nine bands of the lean: $1C, $39, $55, $71, $8E, $AA, $C6, $E3, $FF. Band 4, $71 to $8D, is centred.
Steps the frame script at ($2F): when the count in $31 runs out, the next pair is a frame (drawn) and the frames it lasts; a frame of $FF stops the script there, and a negative count stops stepping.

The in-run's points at ($2F), five bytes each: once the skier passes the first byte's x, his y is set to the second, the frame to the third, the acceleration to the fourth and the slope to the fifth. A zero ends them.

The flight's distance: until the speed in $22-$23 has fallen to 40, it is added to the distance ($1F-$21, metres in $21), and the speed falls by the drag of the lean's band (drag_table), least when centred; the worst lean reached is kept in $40 (lean_size). The skier's shadow, sprite 5 with shape $23, sits below him by the speed less 40, so it closes on him as the landing nears; the distance is drawn in the close-up (inset_distance).
Landed: the shadow off.
The speed lost each frame, in 256ths, by the lean's band: 21, 19, 17, 15, 14 centred, 15, 17, 19, 21.
How far each band is from the centre: 3, 2, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, the index into lean_penalties.

The score screen: sounds stopped, the screen and sprites off, sound 0 (the tune), the light blue text screen ($1C set) unpacked from score_list, and the figures printed: the distance, three times it for the distance points, the style points ($3E-$3F) and their total. A total higher than the player's best (the six characters at +$10 in the record) replaces it. Then the screen on, and in competition a wait of 30 frames and for fire.

Draws frame $41 unless the count in $43 is still running: the small skier's sprite pointer from frame_sprites, and, unless the hill is showing (the bitmap's first byte at $A000 is $69), the close-up: its 30 bitmap cells into rows 2 to 6, columns 30 to 35 ($A370 on), and its 32 cells of sprite shapes into $8F00-$8FFF for sprites 1 to 4. In both, a cell of 8 bytes is stored as is, or as the single byte $33: plain background ($55) in the bitmap, empty in the sprites. After a close-up, none for 4 frames ($43).

The small skier's sprite shape for each of the 31 frames: $1E for frame 0, crouched on the in-run; $10-$13 down the in-run's slopes; $14 the take-off, $15 flying; $25, $25, $20 for frames 7 to 9, leans that the missed take-off's tumble also passes through; $18, $19, $19, $1A the falls (10 to 13); $1B, $1C, $1C the landing; $1D arms up; then the other leans, 18 to 30.

The in-run's points for ramp_script: past x $52, y $38 and frame 1; past $5A, frame 2 on the steep part; past $C0, frame 3; past $E8, frame 4; past $F6, the lip, frame 0, level, with no acceleration. Then a zero.
The frame for each band of the lean when the stick works up and down: $1B, $1E, $1D, $1C, 6 centred, 7, 8, 9, $15.
The frame for each band when the stick works left and right: $16, $14, $13, $12, 6 centred, $17, $18, $19, $1A.
A good landing's frames: 14 and 15 for ten frames each, then 16 for 120, then $FF.
A fall's frames: 10, 11, 12 for ten frames each, then 13 for 120, then $FF.
The missed take-off's tumble: frames 8 to 13, five frames each, then $FF.
For each of the 31 frames, the close-up's two parts for draw_frame: the sprite cells' address, then the bitmap cells'. Frames 0 to 4, on the in-run, have none.
The first frame's sprite cells' high byte; the table's high bytes are read one on from frame_parts.
Each frame's bitmap cells' address, two on from frame_parts, read with frame_cells_hi.
The bitmap cells' addresses' high bytes, three on from frame_parts.
The table's entries for frames 16 to 30.
Steps the script pointer at $2F-$30.
The hill's packed parts for unpack_list: bitmap, screen, colours, then a zero.
The landing slope's packed parts: bitmap, screen, colours, then a zero.
Prints a number in $16-$17 as "123.4" at ($14): the whole part in $17 in hundreds (left out under 100), tens and units, a point, and the fraction in $16 as tenths (divided by 26).
X as a digit character at ($14),Y.
The distance in the close-up, under the skier at $AAF8: the tens and units of the metres in $17, a point and the tenths of $16, each digit a cell of six bytes from digit_cells.
Copies digit X's six bytes from digit_cells into the bitmap at ($14).
The point's six bytes.
Moves ($14) on a cell, eight bytes.
The digits 0 to 9 for the close-up's readout, six bytes (six lines of a cell) each, in multicolour pixel pairs.
The decimal point's six bytes.
The score screen's packed parts: the text and its colours, then a zero.
The score screen's text, packed for the screen at $8000: SKI JUMP SCORE, DISTANCE - and METERS, DISTANCE POINTS, STYLE POINTS with its plus, a rule under it, and TOTAL POINTS.
The score screen's colours, packed, to $D800: white text.
A step of the 24-bit shift register at random_seed: the new bit is bit 0 of $1CF1 exclusive-ored with its bit 5, shifted in at the top.
The random number's three bytes; the drift reads the first.
The random number's middle byte.
The random number's last byte, whose bits 0 and 5 make the next bit.

The hill, the first scene, packed for unpack_stream: the bitmap of the top 24 rows ($A000-$BDFF), the tower and the in-run against the mountains; its first 544 bytes fill rows 0 to 2. Its first byte unpacked, $69 at $A000, is how draw_frame knows the hill is showing.
The hill's bitmap from row 2 to row 3: the stream runs on across the memory map's edge at $4000.
The hill's bitmap from row 3 to row 9.
The hill's bitmap from row 9 to row 14.

The sound engine's six slots, 32 bytes each, a sound playing in each: +0 the SID voice it plays on (0 to 2), bit 7 set when the slot is idle; +1-2 the script's address; +3 the frames until its next step; +4 a loop count; +5-6 its return stack's pointer; +8 to +14 its copy of the voice's seven registers (frequency, pulse width, control, attack-decay, sustain-release); +15 a flag that restarts the envelope; +16 its transposition; +17 a fine tuning; +18-21 a frequency slide (step, count, rate); +22-25 a pulse-width sweep (step, period, count). The file holds leftover bytes here, which stop_all clears.
Slot 0's script address (+1 and +2), the base start_sound writes each slot's through.
The script address's high byte.
Slot 0's count of frames to its next step (+3).
Slot 0's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep (+16 to +25), which start_sound clears for the slot it starts.
Slots 2 and 3.
Slots 4 and 5.
The slot count of sound_step's loops.
One byte for each SID voice: set once a slot has written the voice this frame, so a slot numbered higher wins a voice over a lower one.
Voice 1's claim.
Voice 2's claim.
Nonzero while the engine runs; start_sound clears it while it writes a slot.
The filter's registers, copied to $D415-$D418 every frame: the cutoff's low and high bytes, the resonance and the voices filtered, the filter mode and the volume.
The cutoff's high byte, for $D416.
The resonance and the voices filtered, for $D417.
The filter mode and the volume, for $D418.
The six slots' return stacks for the scripts' calls, 16 bytes each.
start_sound's copies of X and Y.
start_sound's copy of Y.
Three bytes nothing reads.
The counters of the two arpeggio routines at $6EC6 and $6EE8, which nothing calls.
The second arpeggio routine's counter.
The S key's switch: a press sets it to 1 when it is 0, and clears it, stopping every sound, when it is not; nothing else reads it. The file holds 0 here, so it takes two presses to stop the sounds.

Starts sound A (100 and above are ignored) from snd_table: its first byte is the slot it plays in, its second the SID voice; the slot's script starts at its third byte on the next step, with the slot's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep cleared. A sound already playing in that slot is cut off.
Steps the slot pointer at $80-$81; nothing calls it.
Steps the script pointer at $82-$83.
Steps the pointer at $86-$87 through a sound's first bytes.
The S key's debounce count, 0 to 2.

The sound engine, once a frame from the interrupt. First the S key, read through CIA 1 (row 1, column 5): pressed after a release, it turns snd_s_key over. The event's start-up makes port A of CIA 1 an input (it writes 0 to $DC02), so the engine's write there drives no row; the key is seen only while joystick 2 is held down, which pulls row 1 low on the same line.
For each of the six slots that is not idle: the frequency slide (snd_slide), the pulse-width sweep, and, when its count of frames runs out, the next step of its script (script_step).
The slide: the rate taken from the count, and the step added to the frequency when it passes zero.

The pulse-width sweep: every frame the step is added to the pulse width, and turned round each time the period runs out. A slip makes it change only the width's low byte: the high byte's add goes to the low byte too, with no INY between.
The slot's frames counted down; at zero its script runs on.

Copies the slots to the SID, from slot 5 down to 0: each voice takes the registers of the highest slot that plays on it, and a slot's restart flag turns the gate off and on again to restart the envelope. Then the filter's four registers.
The SID's three voices' register addresses, $D400, $D407 and $D40E.
The voices' register addresses' high bytes, read one on from sid_voices.
Stops every sound: the slots and their stacks cleared, each slot idle with its stack pointer set, volume 15 with the low-pass mode and nothing filtered, and the SID's voice registers cleared.
The six slots' stack addresses.
Writes 0 to the SID's registers $D400-$D415.
An arpeggio: sets the slot's transposition from the next of 16 steps in snd_arp_table_one. Nothing calls it.
Its 16 transpositions in semitones.
Another, for two slots side by side, from snd_arp_table_two. Nothing calls it either.
Its 16 transpositions.

Runs a slot's script from ($82) until it waits. A byte under $80 is a note: its pitch (set_note), then a byte of how many frames it lasts, and the gate on with the envelope restarted. From $80 a command, its number in the low seven bits, through snd_commands; numbers above 28 stop the sound (cmd_stop).
Steps past a command's last byte and runs the next.
An RTS after snd_continue that nothing reaches.
A note: its pitch, its length, the gate on.
Steps past the length, then sets the restart flag and the gate on.

The 29 commands' routines: 0 set the loop count, 1 loop to an address while the count lasts, 2 start another sound, 3 call machine code, 4 jump to an address, 5 call a part of a script, 6 return from it, 7 end, 8 stop, 9 transpose, 10 tune, 11 jump to machine code, 12 a note with a pulse width, 13 a tied note (no new envelope), 14 the gate off for a time, 15 attack-decay and sustain-release, 16 the waveform and envelope, 17 the pulse width, pulse waveform and envelope, 18 a raw frequency for a time, 19 the slide off, 20 the sweep, 21 the slide, 22 the volume, 23 the resonance, 24 the cutoff, 25 the filter mode, 26 the voices filtered, 27 cutoff, mode and resonance from three bytes, 28 cutoff, resonance and routing, and mode.
The command routines' high bytes, read one on from snd_commands.
Command 11: jumps to the machine code at the next two bytes; its RTS ends the slot's step.
Command 3: calls the machine code at the next two bytes, then goes on with the script.
Jumps through $84-$85.
Back from the machine code to the next command.
Command 7: the slot goes idle.
Command 8, and any number above 28: the slot's registers cleared, the gate left on with no waveform, and two frames later the end command at snd_end_byte.
Command 7 ($87), where cmd_stop points the script.

Sets the slot's frequency from a note byte: the high four bits the octave, the low four the semitone, plus the slot's transposition, from note_freqs shifted right once for each octave under 7; 15 gives the highest frequency, $FFFF, for noise. The slot's fine tuning is added.

The SID frequencies of 24 semitones from C in the top octave: C is $430F, which is 1046.5 Hz on an NTSC machine and two-thirds of a semitone flat on a PAL one, as in the opening ceremony's and the menu's tables.
The frequencies' high bytes, read one on from note_freqs.
Eight bytes of code nothing reaches: a read, a step and a read.
Command 16: the control byte (waveform and gate), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 17: the pulse width, then the pulse waveform with the gate ($41), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 18: a frequency of two bytes, then a length and the gate on.
A note's length, then the gate on.
Command 4: the script goes on at the next two bytes.
Command 1: the loop count less one; until it reaches 0 the script goes back to the next two bytes' address, then on past them.
Command 0: sets the loop count.
Command 2: starts another sound, often the other voices of a tune.
Command 5: pushes the address after the command onto the slot's stack and goes to the next two bytes' address.
Command 6: back to the address on the slot's stack.
Command 9: the slot's transposition, in semitones.
Command 10: the slot's fine tuning, added to every frequency.
Command 22: the volume, the low four bits of $D418.
Command 24: the filter's cutoff, high byte.
Command 25: the filter mode, the high four bits of $D418.
Command 26: which voices go through the filter, the low four bits of $D417.
Command 23: the resonance, the high four bits of $D417.
Command 27: the cutoff from the first byte and the top bit of the second, the mode from the second's low four bits and the cutoff's low bits from its high four, then the resonance and routing.
Two bytes the filter commands work in.
The filter command's second byte, kept while it works.

Command 21: the slide's rate (255 for every frame) and its step of two bytes, added to the frequency at that rate: the rate is taken from a count each frame, and each time the count passes zero the step is added.
Command 20: the sweep's period and its step.
A note command no table entry reaches: pitch, length, gate.
Command 13: a new pitch and length with no new envelope, the notes tied.
A pulse-width command no table entry reaches.
Command 15: attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 14: the gate off, and a wait of the next byte's frames.
Command 12: a note with the pulse width's high byte, then its length.
Command 19: the slide stopped.
Command 28: the cutoff's high byte, the resonance and routing, and the mode.
The addresses of the event's 31 sounds, by number, for start_sound. Each is a slot, a SID voice and a script.
The sounds' addresses' high bytes, read one on from snd_table.
Sounds 1 to 4 and 12 to 24, which the event doesn't have: slot 0, voice 2, and a stop.

Sound 0, the event's tune, on the hill before the first jump and on the score screen: it starts sounds 29 and 30 for the melody and its harmony, and plays voice 0's own low pulse note, 16 frames on and 10 off, round and round.
Sound 29, the tune's melody on voice 1: a triangle note sliding down, four times, then pulse notes in threes, the last of each held long, round and round.
Sound 30, the tune's harmony on voice 2, a shade sharp (fine tuning 15): the melody's rhythm on lower notes, after a wait of 160 frames each time round.
Sound 10, after a jump under 62 metres: noise on voice 0, rising a little, then held.
Sound 11, after a jump of 62 metres or more: noise on voice 0, rising a little, then held for 255 frames, with sounds 25 and 26.
Sound 26, the long jump's fanfare on voice 2, after a wait of 64 frames: a filtered sawtooth, five quick notes on one pitch, down and back twice, and a long higher note.
Sound 25, with the long jump: short bursts of noise on voice 1 in a quick rhythm, after waits of 22 and 64 frames.
Sound 5, the skis on the in-run: filtered noise on voice 2 at the top of its range, sliding down.

Sound 6, the wind in flight from the take-off: filtered noise on voice 2 sliding down and up, round and round until the score screen stops every sound. The landing's and the fall's sounds, in higher slots, take its voice while they play.
Sound 7, a good landing: a short noise on voice 2 sliding up.
Sound 8, a fall: filtered noise on voice 2 sliding up, then down, with sound 28.
Sound 28, the fall's triangle note on voice 1 sliding down.
Sound 27, with the missed take-off: four frames' pause on voice 1, then the falling triangle note of sound 28.
Sound 9, the missed take-off: a short noise on voice 2, rising a little, with sound 27.
Three bytes after the last sound that nothing reads.

The small skier's 24 sprite shapes, which the start-up copies to $8400-$89FF (pointers $10 to $27): shapes $10 to $13 down the in-run, $14 the take-off, $15 flying, $16 and $17 which no frame uses, $18 to $1A the falls, $1B and $1C the landing, $1D arms up, $1E crouched, $1F a lean.
Shapes $20 to $27, the leans, the shadow ($23) among them.
The file's last 119 bytes, after the shapes: a leftover fill that nothing reads.
